name: Alabama Hills National Scenic Area BLM Dispersed Camping (Movie Road)

management_agency.name: Bureau of Land Management - Bishop Field Office

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - Free BLM Dispersed Camping Permit required online (zero fee)
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 days maximum stay within any 28-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed camping is restricted to designated campsites marked with campsite posts along Movie Road corridor to protect fragile desert ecology. Driving off-road prohibited.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Pack-out mandatory or deep cat-hole (6 inches deep in sandy soil, 200ft from washes). Portable toilet or WAG bags strongly encouraged due to high visitor pressure.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace. No trash receptacles; all garbage must be packed out to Lone Pine disposal sites.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Bring your own firewood. Gathering brush, sage, or wood on BLM land in Alabama Hills is strictly illegal.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Free California Campfire Permit required (available online at readyforwildfire.org). Must use metal fire pan or existing designated ring. Have shovel and 5 gallons of water on site.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Stage 1 and Stage 2 fire bans enforced during high wind and summer dry seasons.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved dirt and washboard gravel road (Movie Road)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Washboard gravel main road; secondary spurs have sandy dips and granite rock outcroppings.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible along main Movie Road; high clearance recommended for rocky site pullouts)

nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low to Moderate (Open desert plain beneath towering Eastern Sierra peaks)

amenities: Unobstructed View of Mount Whitney (14,505 ft)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 65-80°F, high Sierra snowpack backdrop, afternoon winds (25-40 mph gusts).
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot (95-104°F), intense desert sun exposure, boondocking challenging without AC.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Ideal season (70-85°F daytime, crisp 40-50°F nights), low wind, clear skies.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cool 45-58°F daytime, freezing nights (25-35°F), dramatic snow-covered Sierra views.

dangers_and_hazards: Severe high desert winds capable of damaging RV awnings and tents
Mojave Rattlesnakes and Great Basin Rattlesnakes active April through October
Dehydration and intense UV solar exposure
Flash flooding in washes during rare desert rainstorms

common_human_made_sounds: Passing photography and vanlife vehicles along Movie Road
Distant highway hum on US-395 (5 miles east)
Occasional military jet training flight from China Lake / Edwards AFB corridor

common_plants_and_trees: Single-leaf Pinyon Pine (Pinus monophylla on higher slopes)

human_demographics_and_culture: Full-time digital nomads, Hollywood film historians, landscape photographers, Mt. Whitney summit climbers, and rock climbers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Paiute and Shoshone oral traditions honor Mount Whitney ('Tumanguya') and the surrounding granite arches as sacred places of ancient ancestral spirits.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: High quartz granite acoustic resonance, profound visual alignment with the highest peak in the contiguous US, extraordinary star density.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Natural granite rock arch perfectly framing Mount Whitney
Riparian stream corridor leading toward Whitney Portal

public_reviews_summary: World-famous boondocking location. Jaw-dropping Mount Whitney views combined with fast 5G cell internet. Requires online BLM permit and staying within designated post sites.
other_data: Bortle Class 2 night sky. 100% solar panel efficiency due to minimal tree obstruction.
